summary: The bill lets companies substantiate recycled-content marketing claims using mass-balance accounting verified by an independent third-party system, bars misleading claims, requires the FTC to update its Green Guides within one year, and gives the FTC exclusive enforcement authority while preempting state rules.

scores.thoughts: The bill establishes federal standards and FTC enforcement for recycled content claims but contains no provisions authorizing, expanding, or reducing any government expenditures or appropriations.
No provisions in the bill address tax rates, credits, deductions, or any tax policy matters.
The legislation concerns marketing claims for recycled materials and has no connection to healthcare policy, coverage, or markets.
Completely unrelated to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions relate to immigration, border policy, or pathways for legal status.
The bill does not address reproductive rights, abortion access, or related regulations.
No references to military, defense budgets, or national security spending.

The bill regulates environmental marketing claims (recycled content) and preempts state laws on the same subject. While it touches on recycling and green claims, it neither expands environmental protections nor limits substantive environmental regulations; it is a consumer-protection measure on truthful advertising.
No provisions affect welfare programs, food assistance, or other safety-net policies.
Unrelated to schools, education funding, or school choice.
No connection to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.
The bill creates civil enforcement by the FTC for deceptive claims but does not address criminal sentencing, policing, or justice reform.
No provisions on tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export policy.
The legislation has no fiscal impact or implications for deficit or debt management.
Completely unrelated to LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
No provisions concerning foreign assistance or international aid.
Unrelated to voting access, election integrity, or electoral procedures.
No provisions on data privacy, technology regulation, or digital oversight.
The bill does not address worker protections, union rights, or employment relations.
No provisions implicate religious exemptions or civil-rights enforcement.
